papers.title: A Miniature Wireless Device for Closed-Loop Auditory Sleep Modulation.
papers.journal: International IEEE/EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering : [proceedings]. International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering
papers.summary: This paper presents a prototype miniature wireless device for closed-loop auditory sleep modulation, integrating polysomnography data acquisition and configurable control. Performance was quantified in freely behaving rats, demonstrating its feasibility for sleep research and therapy.

papers.title: Sleep stage classification using instantaneous heart and breathing rates with a TCN-BiGRU-SE model.
papers.summary: This study develops a TCN-BiGRU-SE deep learning model using instantaneous heart and breathing rates for sleep staging. It achieves 82.19% accuracy and Kappa 0.74 on SHHS, and 80.44% accuracy and Kappa 0.70 on MESA, outperforming traditional approaches.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation for EEG-FM under Fixed Computational Budgets
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether updating only 9% of parameters in EEG foundation models via self-supervised adaptation can align representations to target tasks under fixed computational budgets. The method improves performance up to 20x AUCPR over linear probing across three clinical EEG datasets, with peak performance requiring only 20-50% of available unlabeled data.

papers.title: Taming foundation model with invariance-oriented pre-training for broad-spectrum EEG analysis across signal-level, brain-state, and brain-health tasks
papers.summary: This paper presents INCEPT, an invariance-oriented EEG foundation model trained on over 11,000 hours of unlabelled clinical EEG, which learns representation-level stability across correlated EEG observations. It ranks first among recent EEG foundation models on 26 of 30 linear-probing metrics and 24 of 30 fine-tuning metrics across ten datasets spanning signal-level, brain-state, and brain-health tasks.

papers.title: From Brain Networks to Sleep Perception: EEG-Derived Global Efficiency is Associated with Subjective Sleep Quality in University Students.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 52 healthy male university students examined associations between EEG-derived global efficiency (GE) during N3 and REM sleep and subjective sleep quality. Higher daytime sleepiness was associated with increased GE during REM in delta, beta, and gamma bands, while higher theta-band GE during N3 was associated with lower insomnia severity, suggesting network topology may partially reflect subjective sleep experience.

papers.title: The Internal Structure of Seizures Reflects Animal-Specific Trajectories of Disease Progression and Circadian Modulation in Epileptic Mice
papers.summary: This study analyzes over one thousand spontaneous seizures from six epileptic mice using a symbolic framework, revealing that seizures follow structured, animal-specific transition rules that evolve over disease progression. Seizure microstructure is modulated by circadian phase, and burst sequences exhibit higher-order temporal dependencies beyond first-order Markov statistics.

papers.title: Toward unified and comprehensive automated electroencephalogram interpretation: a multicentre development and validation of an electroencephalogram foundation model.
papers.summary: This multicentre study developed and validated MORGOTH, an EEG foundation model for broad clinical interpretation across diverse tasks and settings. MORGOTH achieved expert-level performance with AUC-ROC scores of 0.86 to 0.98 across 17 EEG findings, outperforming at least 90% of experts on three of seven multi-expert-annotated datasets and matching or exceeding expert consensus in inter-rater reliability.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Ear-EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interface: A Systematic Comparison and Design Insights.
papers.summary: This study benchmarked 23 deep neural network architectures for ear-EEG-based mental imagery classification, adapting them from scalp-EEG and evaluating under a unified framework. FBLightConvNet achieved the highest accuracy and outperformed CSP-LDA on all recording days, while many state-of-the-art scalp-EEG models failed to generalize, providing design insights for lightweight ear-EEG BCIs.

papers.title: CViT-ESP: Lightweight Pre-trained Vision Transformers for EEG-based Epileptic Seizure Prediction
papers.summary: This study presents CViT-ESP, a framework using pre-trained Vision Transformers with custom CNN front-ends for EEG-based seizure prediction, validated on patient-independent benchmarks. The best architecture achieved a maximum average AUC of 76.4%, improving over prior models' 69.0%, demonstrating a robust and resource-efficient approach.

papers.title: NTSM: Neurophysiology-Guided Tri-Stream Selective State Space Model for Real-Time Driver Fatigue Detection with EEG-EOG Signals.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: This paper proposes NTSM, a neurophysiology-guided tri-stream architecture using Mamba-based selective State Space Models for driver fatigue detection from EEG-EOG. It achieves linear complexity, a COR of 0.8738 on SEED-VIG, and 92.95% accuracy on cross-dataset validation, with an 8.19x inference acceleration over a Transformer baseline.

papers.title: An EEG-Based Evaluation of Antidepressant Effects of Ketamine Enantiomers and Metabolites in Monkeys.
papers.summary: This mini-review summarizes a study by Iwamura et al. that used EEG in a primate model to compare how ketamine enantiomers and metabolites affect brain activity, discussing implications for understanding ketamine-based antidepressant treatments.

papers.title: Predicting Nitrogen Narcosis Using the Electroencephalogram (EEG) Recorded From Experienced Divers.
papers.summary: This study uses EEG features and machine learning to detect nitrogen narcosis in divers. Linear discriminant analysis achieved MCC 0.50 and 82% accuracy on a test set, with delta-band features over midline electrodes being most important.

papers.title: Neferine improves sleep quality in chronically sleep-deprived mice by antagonizing OXRs in noradrenergic and serotonergic neurons.
papers.summary: This study found that neferine (NEF), a bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid, improves sleep quality in chronically sleep-deprived mice by antagonizing orexin receptors (OXRs) in noradrenergic and serotonergic neurons. NEF increased delta power ratio and reduced sleep fragmentation, suppressed LC and DRN neuronal activity, and decreased norepinephrine and serotonin levels.

papers.title: Evaluation of MPEG-4 AAC Audio Codec Using EEG and EMG Signals for Use with DICOM® Neurophysiology.
papers.summary: This study evaluated MPEG-4 AAC audio codec for compressing EEG and EMG signals, using PRD, PSD, and expert opinion. Results showed significant signal quality decline and gamma/beta band changes, indicating audio codecs are inadequate for neurophysiology compression.

papers.title: DMG-GCN: A Dynamic Microstate-Guided Graph Convolutional Network for EEG Cognitive Workload Decoding in Air Traffic Control.
papers.summary: This paper presents DMG-GCN, a dynamic microstate-guided graph convolutional network for EEG-based cognitive workload decoding in air traffic control. The model achieved 80.30% accuracy and 78.63% F1-score in cross-subject evaluations, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines and providing interpretable brain network patterns.

papers.title: Predicting Only from Selected Evidence: A Tempered Product-of-Experts Bottleneck for Auditable EEG Diagnosis
papers.summary: The paper introduces tPoE-EIB, a tempered product-of-experts evidence-information bottleneck head for EEG backbones that restricts predictions to selected evidence. It preserves competitive balanced accuracy across six diagnosis settings and improves selection-faithfulness over post-hoc explanations.

papers.title: Neural correlates of location-response compatibility in an immersive virtual-reality Attention Network Test: a multiverse electroencephalography analysis
papers.summary: This study examines location-response compatibility in a VR Attention Network Test using EEG with a multiverse analysis. The N2pc-window posterior lateralisation showed consistent incompatibility effects across 192 preprocessing branches, while behavioural differences were not reliable.

papers.title: Manifold representation learning for Alzheimer's disease detection with EEG-based functional brain connectivity.
papers.summary: The study proposes a deep manifold representation learning network (CAE-Transformer) for Alzheimer's disease detection using EEG-based functional brain connectivity. It achieved 98.50% accuracy and 99.49% sensitivity in a single-center dataset, with the alpha frequency band showing the highest diagnostic performance.

papers.title: GLSTNet: A Global-Local Spatial Relations and Temporal Dynamics Network for EEG-Based Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: GLSTNet integrates global-local spatial relations and temporal dynamics for EEG-based emotion recognition, achieving high accuracy on DEAP and SEED datasets in both subject-dependent and subject-independent settings.

papers.title: Assessing the performance of artificial intelligence in detecting electrographic status epilepticus when human experts often disagree.
papers.summary: This study evaluated an AI algorithm for detecting electrographic status epilepticus in point-of-care EEG, comparing its performance against human experts. The AI showed higher sensitivity but slightly lower specificity than individual reviewers, highlighting challenges in defining reference standards due to interrater variability.

papers.title: High-accuracy EEG-based driver fatigue detection using feature-coupled tensor decomposition for multimodal brain connectivity analysis.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a Feature-Coupled Tensor Decomposition (FCTD) framework for multimodal brain connectivity analysis in EEG-based driver fatigue detection. It integrates covariance, phase-locking value, and information flow metrics, achieving high accuracies of 99.42% and 93.62% on two public datasets, while noting challenges in cross-subject generalization.

papers.title: Towards Balanced Bias-Variance With SincDualFormer: A Dual-Scale Sinc-Filterbank Transformer Model With SR-BandMix Augmentation for Motor Imagery BCI.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: This paper introduces SincDualFormer, a dual-scale Sinc-filterbank transformer model with SR-BandMix augmentation for motor imagery EEG decoding. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracies on BCI Competition IV-2a (82.14%) and IV-2b (87.93%) datasets, demonstrating robust performance with improved bias-variance trade-offs.

papers.title: Granger connectivity and graph-theoretical analysis of scalp EEG across the preictal to ictal transition for presurgical evaluation.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This study combined Electric Source Imaging with Granger causality and hubness centrality on high-density EEG to localize the epileptogenic zone. Connectivity analyses during the preictal phase showed higher concordance (91% lateralization, 73% localization) than the ictal phase, particularly in temporal and frontal lobe epilepsy.

papers.title: The functional significance of EEG phase synchronization networks during information integration of left and right visual fields
papers.summary: This preprint investigates EEG phase synchronization networks during visual hemifield integration using a data-driven network analysis. It identified broadband synchronization networks under high integration demands, with associations to behavioral performance.

papers.title: A CNN-BiLSTM-GRU and attention-integrated hybrid network for epileptic seizure detection.
papers.summary: This paper develops a hybrid network combining CNN, Bi-LSTM, GRU, and attention mechanisms for epileptic seizure detection from EEG signals. The model achieves 99.23% accuracy with balanced sensitivity and specificity on the UCI dataset, offering a reliable automated detection method.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral power alterations following traumatic brain injury: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical and injury-related moderators.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified resting-state EEG spectral power changes after traumatic brain injury. TBI was associated with increased theta power relative to controls (g=0.50), moderated by TBI etiology and sex, though heterogeneity and publication bias were present.

papers.title: Closed-loop EEG-based neurofeedback and brain-computer interface interventions for mental health: a review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided review examined closed-loop EEG-based neurofeedback and BCI interventions for mental health published since 2021, identifying 25 studies. It reports technical feasibility and emerging therapeutic potential, but notes that the evidence base remains preliminary due to many small pilot or feasibility studies.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity in Young Adults With Clinically Diagnosed Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Self-Reported Habitual Short Sleep: An Alpha-Band Network Analysis.
papers.summary: The study compared resting-state EEG functional connectivity between young adults with generalized anxiety disorder and habitual short sleep (GAD+HSS) and healthy controls. Significant group differences were confined to the alpha-band wPLI network, with stronger connectivity, higher global efficiency, and lower path length in the GAD+HSS group.

papers.title: Theta-range SEEG stimulation for intracranial mapping: extending conventional 1-Hz and 50-Hz protocols.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This study prospectively compared theta-range (7 Hz) SEEG stimulation with conventional 1-Hz and 50-Hz protocols in 25 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, analyzing 1,408 temporal lobe stimulations. They found that 7-Hz stimulation elicited more afterdischarges and clinical signs than 1-Hz at matched parameters, and provided complementary information for temporal lobe mapping, supporting the exploration of intermediate stimulation frequencies.

papers.title: A deep learning approach to mild cognitive impairment detection from electroencephalogram signals.
papers.summary: This study developed an LSTM-based deep learning model to classify mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from EEG signals, achieving 98.14% accuracy on a public dataset. The model outperformed KNN and SVM, demonstrating potential for noninvasive and scalable cognitive health assessments.

papers.title: Parallel electrophysiological and prefrontal hemodynamic alterations during stroop task performance in major depressive disorder: a simultaneous EEG-fNIRS study.
papers.summary: This study used simultaneous EEG and fNIRS during a Stroop task to compare patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) to healthy controls. MDD patients showed impaired behavioral performance alongside altered ERPs, oscillatory activity, and prefrontal hemodynamics, indicating parallel electrophysiological and hemodynamic abnormalities in executive control.

papers.title: Wireless Electroencephalography in Research on Children With Developmental Disabilities: Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped 64 studies on wireless EEG use in children with developmental disabilities, finding ADHD and autism as most studied, with consumer-grade devices dominating and major gaps in data quality reporting.

papers.title: Application of non-invasive electroencephalogram-based brain-computer interfaces in post-stroke hand function rehabilitation.
papers.summary: This review outlines EEG-based BCI rehabilitation for post-stroke hand dysfunction, describing motor imagery and SSVEP paradigms that improve upper limb function via neuroplasticity, but notes challenges like low signal-to-noise ratio and BCI blindness.

papers.title: EEG and ECG Wearable Biosensor-Based Affective State Analysis Using Deep Learning over 6G IoT Healthcare Networks.
papers.summary: This study proposed a framework for EEG- and ECG-based affective state analysis over 6G IoT networks, using an attention-based deep learning model for EEG emotion recognition (90.93% accuracy) and ResNet50 for ECG stress classification. Ray tracing simulations demonstrated feasibility for integrating wearable biosensor-based affective computing into 6G healthcare communication.

papers.title: State-Programmable Conductive and Reactivatable Bio-Adhesive for High-Fidelity Epidermal Biointerfaces.
papers.summary: This paper reports a state-programmable graft interpenetrating network (g-IPN) that forms a printable and reactivatable conductive adhesive (RCA) for epidermal biointerfaces. The RCA achieves high conductivity, state-dependent adhesion, and reversible viscoelasticity, enabling stable EEG and pulse recordings with lower impedance than traditional gels.

papers.title: From Neurovascular Compression to Neural Hyperexcitability: Integrating Microanatomy, Electrophysiology, and Computational Neuroscience to Understand Trigeminal Neuralgia and Hemifacial Spasm.
papers.summary: This review integrates microanatomical, electrophysiological, and computational evidence to explain how neurovascular compression leads to trigeminal neuralgia and hemifacial spasm. It highlights focal demyelination, ion channel redistribution, ephaptic transmission, and computational models that link these mechanisms to clinical manifestations.

papers.title: Associations between illness perceptions, reported symptoms, and gastric electrophysiology in functional dyspepsia and chronic nausea and vomiting syndrome
papers.summary: This study examined associations between illness perceptions, symptoms, mental health, and gastric electrophysiology in 309 patients with functional dyspepsia or chronic nausea and vomiting syndrome. Illness perceptions were strongly correlated with worse symptoms, quality of life, and mental health, and mediated the relationship between mental health and gastrointestinal symptoms, with some associations to gastric electrophysiology phenotypes.

papers.title: A ballooning family: A review of models of the hemodynamic response in blood oxygen level dependent (BOLD) images.
papers.summary: This review examines the balloon model family for the hemodynamic response in BOLD fMRI, covering classical variants, extensions (viscoelasticity, autoregulation, multicompartment), and integrative frameworks like dynamic causal modeling and EEG-fMRI. It concludes the balloon model is a flexible family of mass-balance models, highlighting its interpretability and limitations in specificity and identifiability.

papers.title: Subchronic PAH Exposure Impacts Cardiac Electrophysiology of the Polar Fish, Navaga Cod (Eleginus nawaga).
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of subchronic (5-8 h) exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons on cardiac electrophysiology of isolated ventricular cardiomyocytes from navaga cod. It found that exposure to water-soluble fraction and 3-methylphenanthrene altered action potential parameters via suppression of sodium current and shortening of action potential duration, with effects distinct from acute exposure, suggesting proarrhythmogenic potential.

papers.title: Medical workup in pediatric first psychotic presentation: real-world diagnostic utility in a large tertiary cohort.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the diagnostic yield of medical workup in 235 children and adolescents with first psychotic presentation. It found that routine extensive testing rarely identified an underlying medical cause, with only urine toxicology and clinically guided neuroimaging/EEG being useful, supporting a selective diagnostic approach.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
